messages.content: Predict one decision in a trust game with a pictured male counterpart and his recorded Mandarin voice. You were told these were real people whose faces, voices and decisions had been collected earlier. The truster starts the game with CNY20, and on a trial chooses either to invest CNY0.5 or keep that CNY0.5. Investing sends the trustee CNY2 after a fourfold increase by the researcher. The trustee may return CNY1 (half of the CNY2) to the truster and keep CNY1, or keep all CNY2 and return nothing. For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. The truster income accumulates; do not assume the initial CNY20 is the current balance. The male face and voice are presented together for2000ms after500ms fixation, and decisions have no time limit. F/J keys were counterbalanced, so output the semantic choice rather than a key. This task has distinct decision stages. A TG1truster first chooses whether to invest. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

You are a 20-year-old female student at Southeast University, studying neither economics nor psychology. The male counterpart shown has an attractive face and an attractive voice. He says “我不喜欢你” (“I don’t like you”), expressing negative social interest. You are currently the truster, choosing whether to invest CNY0.5. You have not yet received this trial’s repayment feedback. This is a condition-level marginal case: exact face/voice identity, accumulated balance, task/round order and earlier personal interaction/practice history are unspecified, rather than assumed absent. Output only keep_0.5 or invest_0.5.
keep_0.5

The truster starts the game with CNY20, and on a trial chooses either to invest CNY0.5 or keep that CNY0.5. Investing sends the trustee CNY2 after a fourfold increase by the researcher. The trustee may return CNY1 (half of the CNY2) to the truster and keep CNY1, or keep all CNY2 and return nothing. For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. The truster income accumulates; do not assume the initial CNY20 is the current balance. The male face and voice are presented together for2000ms after500ms fixation, and decisions have no time limit. F/J keys were counterbalanced, so output the semantic choice rather than a key. This task has distinct decision stages. A TG1truster first chooses whether to invest. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

The truster starts the game with CNY20, and on a trial chooses either to invest CNY0.5 or keep that CNY0.5. Investing sends the trustee CNY2 after a fourfold increase by the researcher. The trustee may return CNY1 (half of the CNY2) to the truster and keep CNY1, or keep all CNY2 and return nothing. For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. The truster income accumulates; do not assume the initial CNY20 is the current balance. The male face and voice are presented together for2000ms after500ms fixation, and decisions have no time limit. F/J keys were counterbalanced, so output the semantic choice rather than a key. This task has distinct decision stages. A TG1truster first chooses whether to invest. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

The truster starts the game with CNY20, and on a trial chooses either to invest CNY0.5 or keep that CNY0.5. Investing sends the trustee CNY2 after a fourfold increase by the researcher. The trustee may return CNY1 (half of the CNY2) to the truster and keep CNY1, or keep all CNY2 and return nothing. For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. The truster income accumulates; do not assume the initial CNY20 is the current balance. The male face and voice are presented together for2000ms after500ms fixation, and decisions have no time limit. F/J keys were counterbalanced, so output the semantic choice rather than a key. This task has distinct decision stages. A TG1truster first chooses whether to invest. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

The truster starts the game with CNY20, and on a trial chooses either to invest CNY0.5 or keep that CNY0.5. Investing sends the trustee CNY2 after a fourfold increase by the researcher. The trustee may return CNY1 (half of the CNY2) to the truster and keep CNY1, or keep all CNY2 and return nothing. For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. The truster income accumulates; do not assume the initial CNY20 is the current balance. The male face and voice are presented together for2000ms after500ms fixation, and decisions have no time limit. F/J keys were counterbalanced, so output the semantic choice rather than a key. This task has distinct decision stages. A TG1truster first chooses whether to invest. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

The trustee may return CNY1 (half of the CNY2) to the truster and keep CNY1, or keep all CNY2 and return nothing. For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

The truster starts the game with CNY20, and on a trial chooses either to invest CNY0.5 or keep that CNY0.5. Investing sends the trustee CNY2 after a fourfold increase by the researcher. The trustee may return CNY1 (half of the CNY2) to the truster and keep CNY1, or keep all CNY2 and return nothing. For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. The truster income accumulates; do not assume the initial CNY20 is the current balance. The male face and voice are presented together for2000ms after500ms fixation, and decisions have no time limit. F/J keys were counterbalanced, so output the semantic choice rather than a key. This task has distinct decision stages. A TG1truster first chooses whether to invest. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

The truster starts the game with CNY20, and on a trial chooses either to invest CNY0.5 or keep that CNY0.5. Investing sends the trustee CNY2 after a fourfold increase by the researcher. The trustee may return CNY1 (half of the CNY2) to the truster and keep CNY1, or keep all CNY2 and return nothing. For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. The truster income accumulates; do not assume the initial CNY20 is the current balance. The male face and voice are presented together for2000ms after500ms fixation, and decisions have no time limit. F/J keys were counterbalanced, so output the semantic choice rather than a key. This task has distinct decision stages. A TG1truster first chooses whether to invest. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

The truster starts the game with CNY20, and on a trial chooses either to invest CNY0.5 or keep that CNY0.5. Investing sends the trustee CNY2 after a fourfold increase by the researcher. The trustee may return CNY1 (half of the CNY2) to the truster and keep CNY1, or keep all CNY2 and return nothing. For the truster an investment followed by CNY1 returned produces a net gain of CNY0.5; no return produces a net loss of CNY0.5. Keeping the CNY0.5 causes no change from that trial. The truster income accumulates; do not assume the initial CNY20 is the current balance. The male face and voice are presented together for2000ms after500ms fixation, and decisions have no time limit. F/J keys were counterbalanced, so output the semantic choice rather than a key. This task has distinct decision stages. A TG1truster first chooses whether to invest. Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.

Only after investing does she see whether CNY1 was returned or the counterpart kept CNY2, then answers a hypothetical question about investing CNY0.5 if she met this same counterpart again; this answer is a hypothetical future intention, not an executed additional transfer. A TG2trustee first predicts whether the truster will invest, using two options rather than a probability. She then sees whether the truster invested CNY0.5. Only after receiving an investment does she choose whether to return CNY1 or keep CNY2. A prediction does not determine whether the other person invests.
